keyFindings.description: Drawing cost is unbounded and runs synchronously on the reader's main thread inside useRenderedMarkdown's layout effect (useRenderedMarkdown.tsx:118). Measured with renderProofMermaidSvg under Bun: a 100-node flowchart (2.4 KB) 1.6 s, 200 nodes (5.2 KB) 3.6 s; the deep review measured 400 nodes (12.4 KB) at 10.7 s in V8 and 800 nodes (25 KB, under the 32,000-character body cap) at 75.8 s in JSC. Any author's comment, ask or message freezes every reader's Inbox or Conversation tab, again on each page load once the 32-entry cache is passed. Fix: keep the draw off the main thread (a Worker) or refuse a source over a measured budget with the existing refusal status and its source open, and prove it with a test that a source over the budget never reaches renderMermaidSvg.

A failed chunk load forgets the attempt, so the next body (a live-view turn re-parses once per frame) imports again and logs console.error again, up to 60 times a second for a streamed turn holding a closed mermaid block.

Pins beautiful-mermaid's private CSS variable --_text; a renderer upgrade that renames it fails the test with no reader-visible change. Assert what the line means: the sheet survives non-empty and loses its @import.
data-mermaid-diagram is read only by MarkdownBody.test.tsx and dispatch-mermaid-status has no rule or reader; select figure.dispatch-mermaid in tests and drop both.

The late-draw machinery (pending Set, PendingDraw, drain loop, two attempt guards, contains check) is a second convention for markdown-engine.ts renderWithEngine's draw-now-or-later-with-cancel; and sanitizeMermaidSvg mixes null and throw, lowercases case-sensitive XML element names so <SVG xmlns=svg> passes the svg check and is cast to SVGSVGElement. Behaviour-neutral; fix in this round, since the deployment allows no deferral.
